newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees lower EU beet sugar crop in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees lower EU beet sugar crop in 1996/97.

text.p: German statistician F.O. Licht estimated European Union (EU) beet sugar output at 16.47 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97 compared with 16.997 million in 1995/96.
In its first estimate for European beet sugar production, Licht pegged the total western European crop at 19.045 million tonnes in raw terms against 18.882 million in 1995/96.
"Beet sugar production in Europe will once again be below the long-term trend this year," Licht said in its report.
Output in line with the trend would have been two million tonnes more than 1995/96 in western Europe.
Licht estimated total European beet output, including eastern and western European countries, at 27.827 million tonnes from 28.573 million in 1995/96.
It said weather conditions had been unfavourable in most EU countries while in some, such as Italy, there had been a drop in the sown area following a cut in national aid.
The total expected EU output was likely to reach 15.4 million tonnes in white value when production from cane in Spain and the French Overseas Departments were added.

German production was seen at 4.19 million tonnes from 4.155 million in 1995/96 while that of France was put at 4.18 million tonnes against 4.60 million. The lower crop in the EU would reduce its export potential, Licht said, but this would help it wind down stocks and comply with GATT export commitments in later years.
"The lower crop may be doubly welcomed in view of the fact that it appears that the level of stocks brought forward from 1995/96 will be considerably higher than had been forecast," Licht said.
First estimates indicated that it may not be an easy task to bring down world production to balance demand and supply.
"If world market prices are not to fall world sugar production will have to come down so as to restore the balance between supply and demand," Licht said.

Production in western European countries outside the EU was expected to be sharply higher, especially in Turkey where the area sown has recovered significantly after a rise in the price paid for beet.
Turkish beet sugar production was put at 1.98 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 1.495 million in the previous season.
